name: Malaysia
genZNote: Malaysia is split in two by the South China Sea — Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo's East Malaysia — which is a perfect metaphor for the country itself: one nation holding together Malay, Chinese, and Indian communities, three major religions, and the Petronas Towers, all at once.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Made up of two geographically separated regions: Peninsular Malaysia (bordering Thailand) and East Malaysia on the island of Borneo (bordering Indonesia and Brunei), separated by the South China Sea.
Tropical rainforest climate, with Borneo's rainforests among the oldest and most biodiverse in the world.
The capital, Kuala Lumpur, is home to the Petronas Twin Towers, once the world's tallest buildings.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: A multi-ethnic society of Malay, Chinese, and Indian communities alongside indigenous groups, especially in Borneo; Malay (Bahasa Malaysia) is the national language.
Islam is the official religion (practiced by the Malay-majority population), while Buddhism, Christianity, and Hinduism are also widely practiced, reflecting its ethnic diversity.
Famous for its diverse cuisine blending Malay, Chinese, and Indian culinary traditions, and major festivals celebrated across communities (Hari Raya, Chinese New Year, Deepavali).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal constitutional monarchy with a unique rotating monarchy: the King (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) is elected every five years from among the hereditary rulers of nine Malay states.
A parliamentary democracy with an elected Prime Minister and bicameral Parliament handling day-to-day governance.
Composed of 13 states and 3 federal territories, including Kuala Lumpur.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant regional hub for electronics and semiconductor assembly and testing, integrated into global tech supply chains.
Growing halal pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry, leveraging its position as a majority-Muslim nation with advanced manufacturing capability.
Strong palm oil-derived biofuel and renewable feedstock research given its position as a top global palm oil producer.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding-era ASEAN member and one of Southeast Asia's more diversified, trade-oriented economies.
Maintains an active role in the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and Commonwealth of Nations, reflecting its historical British colonial ties.
Balances relationships between major powers, with strong trade links to China, the US, and neighbouring ASEAN states.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: Home to a significant ethnic Indian (largely Tamil-origin) community, forming a deep, longstanding people-to-people bond with India.
India and Malaysia share an 'Enhanced Strategic Partnership' with growing trade, defence, and palm oil trade ties (Malaysia is a top source of India's palm oil imports).
Cultural links are reflected in Hindu temples, Deepavali celebrations, and strong diaspora business and cultural connections.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A diversified, upper-middle-income economy built on electronics manufacturing, palm oil, natural gas, and rubber.
One of the world's top two palm oil producers and exporters, alongside Indonesia.
A significant regional financial and logistics hub, especially through its Islamic finance industry.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The Petronas Twin Towers and Kuala Lumpur's modern skyline.
A unique multi-ethnic, multi-religious society across Malay, Chinese, and Indian communities.
Being one of the world's top two palm oil producers.
Borneo's ancient rainforests and rich biodiversity.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Malaysian Ringgit (MYR).
A diversified upper-middle-income economy, strong in electronics manufacturing, palm oil, and natural gas.
One of the world's largest exporters of palm oil and semiconductors.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to some of the world's oldest rainforests, spanning Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo (Sabah and Sarawak).
Rich biodiversity includes orangutans and pygmy elephants in Borneo; faces palm-oil-related deforestation pressures alongside conservation initiatives.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: A historic hub of maritime trade in Southeast Asia; came under British colonial administration.
Achieved independence in 1957 (as Malaya) and formed the Federation of Malaysia in 1963, uniting Malaya, Singapore, Sabah, and Sarawak (Singapore separated in 1965).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1957 independence; 1963 formation of the Federation of Malaysia.
A federal constitutional monarchy with a rotating monarchy (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) elected among state rulers every five years — a distinctive feature of its system.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Badminton is a major national sport with strong international success.
The Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur were once the world's tallest buildings.
A multicultural society blending Malay, Chinese, and Indian traditions, reflected in its cuisine and festivals.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of ASEAN.
Member of the UN, the Commonwealth of Nations, and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Malaysia is a multi-ethnic Southeast Asian federal constitutional monarchy with a unique rotating kingship, split between Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo.
keyFacts: Capital: Kuala Lumpur. Currency: Malaysian Ringgit.
Federal constitutional monarchy; King elected every 5 years from 9 hereditary state rulers.
One of the world's top two palm oil producers.
Significant ethnic Indian community; strong India cultural and trade ties.
commonConfusion: Malaysia's monarch is elected on rotation among state rulers every five years — it is not a single hereditary line like most monarchies.

highYieldFacts: Malaysia: federal constitutional monarchy with a uniquely rotating, elected kingship.
One of the world's top two palm oil producers, alongside Indonesia.
India-Malaysia: Enhanced Strategic Partnership; large ethnic Indian diaspora.
commonTraps: Assuming Malaysia's monarchy is hereditary in a single family — it rotates among 9 state rulers.
Confusing Malaysia's two separated regions (Peninsular and Borneo/East Malaysia).
mustRemember: Malaysia: rotating constitutional monarchy, top palm oil producer, deep India diaspora and trade links via Tamil-origin community.
